title: Node frontend (bundled web app)
confidence_notes: package.json with a build script and a bundler or framework dependency is the signal. If package.json has express, fastify, koa, hono or nest and no bundler, it is service-api instead. If there is a bin field and no index.html or pages, it is cli-tool. A monorepo (workspaces field, pnpm-workspace.yaml, turbo.json) matches per package; report the app package, not the root. Next.js and other SSR apps are node-frontend plus service-api; measure Lighthouse against the built output, not the dev server.

default_cards.title: Failing unit tests (vitest JSON reporter)

measure.command: [ -x node_modules/.bin/vitest ] || exit 3; out=$(npx --no-install vitest run --reporter=json 2>/dev/null); printf '%s' "$out" | python3 -c 'import json,sys; d=json.load(sys.stdin); f=d["numFailedTests"]; f = f if (f or d.get("success", True)) else 1; print("METRIC tests_failed=%d" % f)'

gaming_risks: test.skip, it.skip, describe.skip, or .todo added; a test file renamed so the include glob misses it
snapshots updated with -u (the __snapshots__ dir is frozen; a snapshot inlined into a non-frozen file is the workaround to look for)
expect(...) assertions replaced by expect.anything() or removed
vitest.config include/exclude narrowed, or a setupFile that mocks the module under test
a run with zero total tests reads as a failure via the success flag, never as clean

default_cards.title: TypeScript errors (tsc --noEmit)

measure.command: [ -x node_modules/.bin/tsc ] || exit 3; npx --no-install tsc --noEmit --pretty false 2>&1 | awk '/error TS[0-9]+:/{n++} END{print "METRIC tsc_errors=" n+0}'

degradation.apply: printf '\nexport const sbDegradation: number = "not a number";\n' >> {{entry_module}}

gaming_risks: // @ts-ignore, // @ts-expect-error, or `as any` casts added
tsconfig strictness lowered (protected path; look for an inline tsconfig override via a new extends file)
a file excluded from the program by moving it to a path outside include
types loosened to unknown/any at module boundaries

default_cards.title: ESLint problems (errors + warnings)

measure.command: [ -x node_modules/.bin/eslint ] || exit 3; npx --no-install eslint . -f json 2>/dev/null | python3 -c 'import json,sys; r=json.load(sys.stdin); print("METRIC lint_errors=%d" % sum(f["errorCount"]+f["warningCount"] for f in r))'

gaming_risks: eslint-disable comments added
.eslintignore or an ignores entry widened
rules turned off in a nested config file in a non-protected directory
code deleted rather than fixed

default_cards.title: Gzipped size of all JS in {{dist_dir}}

measure.command: npm run build --silent >/dev/null 2>&1 || exit 1; printf 'METRIC bundle_gzip_bytes=%s\n' "$(find {{dist_dir}} -type f -name '*.js' -exec cat {} + | gzip -9 -n | wc -c | tr -d ' ')"

degradation.apply: python3 -c "import random; random.seed(7); print('export const sbBloat = [' + ','.join(str(random.random()) for _ in range(40000)) + '];')" >> {{entry_module}}

gaming_risks: code moved from JS into a JSON, WASM, or CSS asset that the glob does not count
a route or feature lazy-loaded so its chunk is still shipped but the goal measures the same files: fine if it is genuinely split, not fine if the chunk was renamed to .mjs
minifier options changed (a config operator; must be declared)
a dependency replaced by a CDN script tag (network at runtime; check index.html)
dead code removed by deleting a feature users rely on (tests and Lighthouse a11y should catch a missing UI)

default_cards.title: Lighthouse performance score, {{page_path}}

measure.command: [ -x node_modules/.bin/lhci ] || exit 3; npm run build --silent >/dev/null 2>&1 || exit 1; rm -rf .lighthouseci; npx --no-install lhci collect --static-dist-dir={{dist_dir}} --url={{page_path}} -n 3 >/dev/null 2>&1 || exit 1; python3 -c 'import json,glob,statistics; s=[json.load(open(f))["categories"]["performance"]["score"] for f in glob.glob(".lighthouseci/lhr-*.json")]; print("METRIC lighthouse_perf=%.3f" % statistics.median(s))'

screen.command: [ -x node_modules/.bin/lhci ] || exit 3; npm run build --silent >/dev/null 2>&1 || exit 1; rm -rf .lighthouseci; npx --no-install lhci collect --static-dist-dir={{dist_dir}} --url={{page_path}} -n 1 >/dev/null 2>&1 || exit 1; python3 -c 'import json,glob; s=[json.load(open(f))["categories"]["performance"]["score"] for f in glob.glob(".lighthouseci/lhr-*.json")]; print("METRIC lighthouse_perf=%.3f" % s[0])'

degradation.apply: python3 -c "import random; random.seed(7); print('export const sbBloat = [' + ','.join(str(random.random()) for _ in range(60000)) + ']; for (let i = 0; i < 2e8; i++) { globalThis.__sb = (globalThis.__sb || 0) + i; }')" >> {{entry_module}}

gaming_risks: content removed from the measured page (a blank page scores 100)
a user-agent or navigator.webdriver sniff that serves a lighter page to headless Chrome
images replaced with placeholders or lazy-loaded below the fold in a way that never loads them
third-party scripts deferred past the measurement window but still required for function
the holdout pages differ from the screened page: an improvement that only lands on {{page_path}} is a page-specific hack

default_cards.title: Lighthouse accessibility score, {{page_path}}

measure.command: [ -x node_modules/.bin/lhci ] || exit 3; npm run build --silent >/dev/null 2>&1 || exit 1; rm -rf .lighthouseci; npx --no-install lhci collect --static-dist-dir={{dist_dir}} --url={{page_path}} -n 1 --settings.onlyCategories=accessibility >/dev/null 2>&1 || exit 1; python3 -c 'import json,glob; s=[json.load(open(f))["categories"]["accessibility"]["score"] for f in glob.glob(".lighthouseci/lhr-*.json")]; print("METRIC lighthouse_a11y=%.3f" % s[0])'

gaming_risks: interactive elements removed instead of labelled
aria attributes added mechanically (aria-label="") that satisfy the audit without helping users
the page rendered empty for the auditor

default_cards.title: Time to interactive, {{page_path}}

measure.command: [ -x node_modules/.bin/lhci ] || exit 3; npm run build --silent >/dev/null 2>&1 || exit 1; rm -rf .lighthouseci; npx --no-install lhci collect --static-dist-dir={{dist_dir}} --url={{page_path}} -n 3 >/dev/null 2>&1 || exit 1; python3 -c 'import json,glob,statistics; s=[json.load(open(f))["audits"]["interactive"]["numericValue"] for f in glob.glob(".lighthouseci/lhr-*.json")]; print("METRIC tti_ms=%.0f" % statistics.median(s))'

degradation.apply: printf '\nfor (let i = 0; i < 3e8; i++) { globalThis.__sb = (globalThis.__sb || 0) + i; }\n' >> {{entry_module}}

gaming_risks: main-thread work moved to a requestIdleCallback that never runs during the audit but still blocks real users later
hydration skipped for the measured route only

noise_sources: headless Chrome timing (Lighthouse recommends the median of 3 to 5 runs; TTI varies 10 to 20% run to run on a laptop)
network stubs and service workers left registered between runs (lhci uses a fresh profile; a custom runner may not)
node_modules hard-link state and bundler caches (.vite, .next/cache) across worktrees
CPU throttling emulation in Lighthouse interacting with a busy host
font and image decoding on first paint
notes: Reuse first: an existing lighthouserc, a size-limit or bundlesize config, or a CI step that reports bundle size is trusted more than these defaults; read package.json scripts for build, test, lint and typecheck names. Fill {{dist_dir}} from the bundler config (dist, build, .next, out), {{page_path}} with a real route (/ is fine), {{entry_module}} with the app entry (src/main.tsx, src/index.ts). The three Lighthouse cards share a build and a collect run each; they are not cached across cards, so if cost matters keep lighthouse_perf and drop tti_ms. Lighthouse and TTI are contention_safe=false. Lighthouse holdout is by page: pick two routes the experimenter is not shown, and treat a gain on the screened route that vanishes on holdout as a page-specific hack. For jest instead of vitest use npx jest --json --silent; the JSON fields (numFailedTests, success) are the same. Snapshot files are frozen; a diff that inlines a snapshot into a test helper is the workaround the judge should look for. dependency gets a warmer prior here than elsewhere because swapping a heavy library for a lighter one is the most common honest bundle-size win.
